chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, ruled regarding a boy against whom a woman testified that he had pushed another boy into a well and killed him, so he accepted the testimony of the woman.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well into which the boy was pushed
key_terms.غُلَامٍ: a boy or youth involved in the case
key_terms.قَضَى: he ruled or issued a judicial decision

ai.seo_question: When can a woman’s testimony be accepted in a legal case according to a hadith from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in a case of homicide involving boys. It indicates that the testimony of a woman was accepted in establishing the facts of the case, highlighting an applied judicial ruling in Shia fiqh.
